base_contract: b-one-sponsor-capability.json; all common ownership, Q3, page boundaries, first-R, service and actual-versus-chosen-environment restrictions remain in force unless the two-active-child extension below is explicitly selected.
preservation: The previous fixed-resident-C3 comparison is correct within its specified action class and is unchanged. This separate artifact applies exactly the same credit-first streaming release to the all-partial control.

same_streaming_rule_for_all_partial.initial: Source AR -1, true source R1/R2/R3 at0/1/2. First A AW0 is qualified by actual first R0 with the entire first source quantum already reserved in both private Q3 FIFOs; first true A W4 uses real payload. B first AW1 is subject to the same first-R and reservation rule.
same_streaming_rule_for_all_partial.second_child: Source R4/R5 at11/13 give A two true words. B's true first-child WLAST14 releases one actual private source slot. Reserve the one remaining source word for both recipients and offer A AW15; source R6 accepts at15, supplying true W16. B second AW16 follows its first real B15.
same_streaming_rule_for_all_partial.tail_preparation: A head service24..H+23 acquires atH+23, usableH+24; B head serviceH+24..2H+23 acquires at2H+23, usable2H+24. Native handshakes enter the one charged global owned-result slot. Old prefix WRITE records survive A21/B27; migration preserves the granted cookie through each tail's B.
same_streaming_rule_for_all_partial.tail_formulas: With G the least eligible even W slot: A_W=G(max(28,H+25)); A_ACK=A_W+1. B_W=G(max(A_W+2,29,2H+25)); B_ACK=B_W+1.
same_streaming_rule_for_all_partial.record_ports: For H1, A native result24 is usable25 and can migrate25 to A's already vacant prefix slot while B's result25 actually replaces the one global slot. This is the same explicitly charged common consume/replace port in the base card. No READY0 value is used as a grant.
same_streaming_rule_for_all_partial.no_hidden_debt: Only physical child length3 is committed; the single missing shared word is covered by both actual reserved slots. The full accepted source obligation remains7, with each unauthorized final tail1 fitting its Q3. Physical WLAST does not retire the original source or logical parent.

single_active_child_finite_comparison.result: all-partial A earlier by2, B unchanged, same makespan33

H3_all_partial_complete_tail.grant_lifetime: A's old prefix real B21 frees its private slot22, so its owned tail result26 can migrate27. B's old prefix real B27 frees its private slot28, so its result29 is also actually acquired and retained without a fourth owned WRITE record. No physical child uses a grant before its usable slot.
H3_all_partial_complete_tail.full_cost: For both methods: sourceAR1/sourceR7, trueW14/null0, each flow3AW and3realB, tailPTWAR2/truePTER2, own prepares6, owned tail captures2/migrations2, WRITE-record capacity3, READ-record capacity2 and exclusive payload slots6. H3 tail head service is6 slots; it is not6 accepted PTE beats.

sponsor_choice_and_bounded_target.symmetry: In this symmetric H3 cold contract, choosing B instead of A as the full sponsor and swapping owner/preparation order yields the correspondingly swapped ACK33/31. The all-partial preparation order can also be swapped. The selected two-slot gain is not evidence that the identity A is special.
sponsor_choice_and_bounded_target.target_bound_with_one_active_child: A cold full sponsor cannot deliver first source R before4, hence first true W is at least6. To finish both 7-word jobs by real ACK33, all14 true W must fill all14 even slots6..32 without an idle. If either job ACK is at most29, that job is finished by W28. At W28 total12 true words have been written, so the other job has only5 words written; its sixth prefix word must be W30 and its seventh word is the separate next-page tail. Its prefix real B31 then permits a tail AW only at32, whose true W is at least34. Contradiction. Thus no one-full-sponsor schedule in this strict one-active-child/registered-B-reuse class can match the target componentwise29/33, independent of sponsor identity.
sponsor_choice_and_bounded_target.bound_limit: This is a finite action/resource timing bound, not total-ACK optimality, not a statement about every AXI pipeline, and not a platform proof. Allowing a tail child AW before the prefix B changes the action class. In particular, the platform's existing outstanding capacity must not be artificially denied to ordinary controls.

stronger_ordinary_countercontrol_with_co.why_included: If the shared architecture allows two physical child descriptors per flow from the same existing outstanding pool, the single-active bound is insufficient. Both methods must receive that allowance. This concrete countercontrol then defeats the selected H3 streaming candidate29/33 without adding payload slots or owned permission records.
stronger_ordinary_countercontrol_with_co.common_extended_resource: Allow at most2 active physical WRITE children per flow, charged against the same common pool of outstanding descriptors, at most4 active across these flows and below8 total. This is a proposed common interface allowance, not proof that the production adapter already supports it. All PA/cookie results still occupy only3 owned WRITE records. One existing native-response register may hold an unowned READY0 result and is charged to both controls; its value cannot authorize an AW.
stronger_ordinary_countercontrol_with_co.policy: Prepare A tail as the actual full sponsor, then use A prefix3+3 and B prefix4+2. Commit B's first4 only after A's first3 really drains, with A's real empty FIFO covering the single missing word. Retain already owned A tail grant for an early tail AW; defer B's second prefix AW until that tail AW is accepted so global AW/W order is legal. Obtain B tail permission after source RLAST; use only its actual owned result, then issue B tail AW before its second prefix B if the common two-child resource is available.

actual_prepare_and_records.A: Cold PTE service0/1/2, actual owned acquisition2, usable3. Global A-tail record remains genuine and usable at tailAW23 while old A-prefix record is retained through real B25. At26 migrate the same tail cookie to A's now vacant private slot; retain it through real tailB27.
actual_prepare_and_records.B: Cold PTE head service22/23/24. Its native response cannot be acquired24 because the sole global owned slot still contains A. Hold native response READY0 until26; it does not count as a lease and does not authorize AW. At26 A migration and actual B-result capture occur using the common consume/replace port; B grant usable27, so tailAW27 is legal. B's old prefix record stays through real B31; tail cookie may migrate32 and stays valid through tailB33.
actual_prepare_and_records.native_busy_cost: The native result hold24..26 is an actual stall; no other cold walk is claimed to run during that hold. There is no additional cold work in these two jobs. A controller lacking the common response holding/capture route must account for that interface restriction, rather than use the result early.
actual_prepare_and_records.peak: Before26: A-prefix, B-prefix, A-tail global. After26: A-tail private, B-prefix, B-tail global. Never4 owned WRITE records. The unowned TL response is explicitly distinct and charged as the common native response register.

stronger_ordinary_countercontrol_with_co.payload_and_order_legality: B prefix4 firstAW11 has3 true resident words; A's first3 has already drained at10, so A can accept the fourth shared word. B true W12 releases its own fourth-word slot, then R4=13 accepts both. R5/R6=15/17 also fit after B true W14/16. A second true W20 releases the last shared source credit, so R7=21 accepts into both Q3 FIFOs. A tail stays behind its own prefix bytes and becomes FIFO head after W24; B tail stays behind prefix bytes through W30. Global AW order above exactly matches W-owner order; every offered field is immutable, every old/new permission coexists within the three-record budget, all per-ID responses remain ordered, and no held R is switched.
stronger_ordinary_countercontrol_with_co.complete_cost: Same sourceAR1/R7, trueW14/null0, total6AW/6realB, tailPTEAR2/truePTER2, own prepares6 and owned captures2/migrations2 as the selected all-partial streaming candidate. No source re-read, no future oracle, no extra payload slot, and no free READY0 authorization. Only the common active-child allowance differs from the strict single-child subcase; it must be offered to both controls.
stronger_ordinary_countercontrol_with_co.scope_verdict: At this common two-child allowance the selected all-partial ACK29/33 is reproduced and improved by ordinary ACK27/33. Consequently the narrow single-child H3 gain cannot be promoted to an independent performance contribution using a production platform that already permits the stronger common action. This does not prove an optimum for redesigned all-partial policies.

final_boundary.positive: Because the all-partial frontier safely starts payload before a cold full sponsor is available, it adds an early admission action and the single-child H3 comparison can turn that action into a small complete-ACK improvement. This corrects any implication that applying the same streaming rule automatically removes every all-partial effect.
final_boundary.negative: H1/H2 tie and H4 is worse even in the single-child contract. A same-budget two-child ordinary countercontrol defeats the selected H3 point when that action is common. The useful action therefore needs a genuinely justified resource/interface restriction or a new full-cost policy comparison; these hand parity points alone do not establish independent novelty or a general benefit.
final_boundary.decision: Retain the exact admission capability and this conditional architecture boundary. Do not launch RTL or expand a phase matrix on this point. Root decides the next distinct mechanism.
final_boundary.execution: Codex hand derivation only; no model, RTL, build, primary search, production changes or board test.
